content: Cefazolin is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It is also commonly administered before and during certain surgical procedures to help prevent infections. This medication belongs to the class of cephalosporin antibiotics. Cefazolin is typically given by injection, either into a vein or a muscle, depending on the specific product and medical condition. It is essential to use this medication exactly as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Before use, inspect the product for any particles or discoloration; do not use it if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Occasionally, it may cause loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, cefazolin may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridium difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of cefazolin may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before using cefazolin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Cefazolin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Additionally, this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefazolin may interfere with certain lab tests, such as Coombs' tests or specific urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms like passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. While using this product, your doctor may order lab tests, such as complete blood counts or kidney function tests, to monitor your progress. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
